chunks: This man here is my brother. He has ninety and nine ewes while I have only one. He demands that I should give him my ewe, and wants to get the better of me in argument.
ai.seo_question: What is the story of the two men and the ewes mentioned in Surah Sad?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a parable where the ninety-nine ewes represent the many sins or worldly attachments of the self, while the single ewe symbolizes the one remaining virtue or the final judgment. The phrase 'عَزَّنِي فِي الْخِطَابِ' (he made himself strong in speech) is understood by scholars like Allamah Tabatabai to indicate an arrogant insistence on his own rightness despite the disparity in their holdings, illustrating the human tendency to justify greed through rhetorical dominance.
